To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the Kelvin-Helmh Holtz instability of an AGN bubble can dissolve the bubble completely on a timescale of ~ 100 Myr in a hot stratfied medium, and that (b) in SPH schemes the thermal energy remains in the bubble, while it is stirred in the surrounding ICM in the other codes.

the numerical treatment of the hydrodynamics has a significant influence on the evolution of the AGN bubbles, and that the choice of the numerical scheme has a small effect on the thermal structure in the ICM.
the numerical schemes have a significant influence on the stability of the bubble and the thermal structure of ICM, while the thermal structure of cluster centre remains almost unaffected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the hydrodynamical scheme affects the outcome of simulations of AGN feedback.
the numerical stability of bubbles inflated by AGN in the intracluster medium and the influence of different numerical schemes.
the physical and numerical stability of AGN bubbles rising in a hot intra-cluster medium (ICM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the numerical schemes used for hydrodynamical simulations are not interchangeable.
the numerical scheme should be chosen to capture the physics of the problem at hand.
all hydrodynamical approaches are able to capture the physics of the problem, but that the numerical approach has a large impact on the outcome of the simulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
numerical instabilities in simulations of AGN feedback are not a problem as long as the numerical schemes are stable in the absence of feedback.
the numerical schemes are not able to capture the Kelvin-Helmhlotz instability of a buoyant bubble in the ICM.
the bubble disruption is a robust result, but that the numerical schemes used to study the bubble disruption are not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the numerical approach can influence the results of simulations of AGN bubbles and their feedback in the ICM.
in order to capture the physics of the interaction of bubbles in the ICM correctly, the numerical scheme needs to capture the Kelvin-Helmh Holtz instability.

numerical schemes that can capture Kelvin-Helmh Holtz instability well, are necessary in order to obtain a realistic description of the mixing between bubbles and the ICM, and to obtain realistic feedback effects.
